quote: Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: Kubient's indemnity covers the Services, the Auction Platform, breach of its representations and warranties (which include the non-infringement warranty in 9(b)(i)) and its acts or omissions, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedures in Section 11; Customer's indemnity is confined to its own misuse, Content/Properties and warranty breach. This meets the preferred position on its material terms.

quote: Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.
rationale: Nothing assigns Customer IP, Content or data to Kubient, no joint ownership is created, and each Party retains its own marks; Kubient's ownership of the Auction Platform is acceptable. Direction of ownership is therefore correct. We note the Agreement lacks an express "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data" statement, which we would add opportunistically rather than as a redline.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 excludes indirect damages but contains no aggregate cap, so both parties' direct liability is unlimited. We have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap.

ops.text: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE AGGREGATE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BETWEEN THE PARTIES UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with standard carve-outs to Section 7

quote: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION, OR LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES
rationale: Section 7 contains only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; there is no aggregate cap of any kind, so our direct liability is unlimited and the fallback (mutual 12-month cap) is not met. We added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' amounts paid or payable between the Parties and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap (the existing carve-outs for indemnity and confidentiality are preserved). Because this is a revenue-share deal in which Customer pays no fees, the cap basis is expressed as amounts paid or payable between the Parties.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

quote: either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction
rationale: Customer may assign to affiliates and M&A successors without consent, other assignments require consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, and there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on Customer's change of control. This meets the preferred position on its material terms; we note only that Kubient's free assignment right is not restricted from transfers to a Customer competitor.

quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient.
rationale: The Agreement is expressly non-exclusive and imposes no sole-supplier or all-requirements obligation on Customer, meeting the preferred position.

quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
rationale: There are no liquidated damages, penalties or minimum termination payments payable by Customer; Kubient simply retains its share of revenue actually generated during the notice period, which is not a Customer-payable penalty.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a licence that Kubient may revoke at will or that excludes our affiliates and the contractors who operate our properties; the licence should end only with the Agreement. We have deleted "revocable" and added affiliates, contractors and successor transferability.

ops.newText: non-transferable, non-assignable license (which extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf, and is transferable to a successor by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets) to access, participate in and use
ops.oldText: non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use

proposal.summary: Delete "revocable" and extend the licence to affiliates, contractors and successors

quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient
rationale: The licence is expressly revocable at Kubient's discretion and excludes affiliates, contractors and any successor, which is walk-away territory under this rule (Section 6(a) also bars third-party access absent Kubient's written approval, so there is no path to add them). We deleted "revocable", extended the grant to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and made it transferable to an M&A successor; termination of the licence remains governed by Section 4(c).

quote: This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer; Section 1 expressly confirms Customer's freedom to use other agents and channels. The Section 6 use restrictions relate to the licensed platform, not to our business activities.

quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
rationale: Customer has a rolling convenience right after a 12-month Initial Term on 90 days' notice, which sits at the fallback (60–90 days), and Kubient's mirror right is also at 90 days' notice, so neither walk-away trigger applies. There is no early-termination fee (Kubient simply keeps revenue-share fees generated during the notice period). We separately propose shortening our notice to 30 days under the renewal rule.

quote: Pursuant to the doctrine of sequential liability, payment from Kubient to Customer shall be made within seven (7) days from Kubient's receipt of payment, regardless of when Customer submits an invoice.
rationale: The Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection or verification right against Customer and no access to our systems, which matches the preferred position (no audit rights). Impressions are measured by Kubient, so our own verification rights over reporting are a separate commercial ask, not a playbook deviation.

quote: This Agreement is governed in all respects by the laws of the State of Delaware without giving effect to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party hereby irrevocably submits for all disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in New York, New York.
rationale: Delaware law with exclusive venue in New York County courts sits within the accepted list (fallback law, preferred venue). Section 8's AAA Commercial Arbitration clause is domestic, not a foreign-seated arbitration, so no walk-away trigger; we note only that Section 8 and 14(a) conflict on forum and that the one-year suit limitation in Section 8 is worth addressing separately.

quote: The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
rationale: There is no most-favoured-nation or price-matching obligation anywhere in the Agreement, and none burdening Customer. Commercial terms sit in the Exhibits; we should confirm no MFN language appears there.

quote: The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit.
rationale: Compensation is a pure revenue share on Services actually engaged under Exhibits, with no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume commitment on Customer, and Customer remains free to sell Inventory elsewhere. Any Exhibit-level minimums should be checked when Exhibits are issued.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or inducement restriction binding Customer, which matches our preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement auto-renews for 1-year terms and the only exit requires 90 days' notice, which exceeds our 30-day preferred (60-day fallback) window. We have reduced Customer's notice to 30 days while leaving Kubient's 90-day notice unchanged.

ops.newText: Customer may elect not to renew, or terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term, upon thirty (30) days written notice to Kubient, and Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer.
ops.oldText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.

proposal.summary: Reduce Customer's non-renewal/exit notice to 30 days

quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions
rationale: Renewal terms are 12 months (acceptable), but the only means of avoiding a renewal is the 90 days' written notice in Section 4(a), which exceeds our fallback window of 60 days. We reduced Customer's non-renewal/exit notice to 30 days and left Kubient's at 90 days. No price-uplift cap is needed here as compensation is a revenue share, so that sub-element is noted only.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4(c) addresses Confidential Information only and gives us no exit help or return of our data. We have added up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer data within 30 days in machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days' assistance).

ops.text: at Customer's request, Kubient shall provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at its then-current rates; within thirty (30) days of termination Kubient shall return to Customer all Customer data, Content and Requests in its possession in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and Kubient shall thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Add transition assistance, data return and deletion certification on termination

quote: (iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.
rationale: Section 4(c) provides only for cessation of Services and return or destruction of Confidential Information; there is no transition assistance and no obligation to return our data (Content, Requests, visitor data held by Kubient) in a usable format, and the "destroy" option risks immediate deletion of data we need. We inserted a transition-assistance, data-return-within-30-days and certified-deletion paragraph; fallback is 90 days' assistance.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Kubient gives express performance, error-free, no-malicious-code, compliance-with-law and non-infringement warranties that run throughout the Term (better than the 90-day preferred period), and the Section 13 disclaimer is expressly subject to "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement", so it does not swallow them. We note the absence of an express re-perform/repair/refund remedy sentence as a sub-element to raise in negotiation rather than a fallback failure, since warranty breach is separately indemnified and a termination trigger.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Vendors that collect and store visitor data for us carry standard cover, and the Agreement has no insurance clause. We have added our standard CGL, E&O and cyber limits with certificates on request; our fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

ops.text: Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient collects, processes or stores Customer data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Kubient shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a Vendor insurance paragraph in the General Provisions

rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance obligation at all, even though Kubient collects, maintains and stores visitor data on our behalf (Section 9(b)(iii)) — walk-away territory for a data-processing vendor. We inserted a short insurance paragraph in the General Provisions with our standard CGL, E&O and cyber limits and certificates on request; fallback is E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
